title: Strength — Dumbbells Intermediate
subtitle: Upper/lower strength split, home dumbbells
coaching_note: You should be picking a weight where the last 2 reps of each set are genuinely hard, not just tiring. If you're cruising through every set, it's too light — tell me and we'll adjust.

exercises.name: Jump Rope (or high knees if no rope)
exercises.form_cue: Light on your feet, small jumps, steady rhythm.
exercises.why: Full-body warm-up that raises heart rate faster than static stretching.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Good Morning
exercises.form_cue: Hands behind head, soft knees, hinge forward from the hips until you feel your hamstrings, stand back up.
exercises.why: Rehearses the hip hinge pattern before you load it with a dumbbell RDL.

phases.name: Lower Body — Heavy
phases.coaching_note: This is the heaviest block of the session — take the full rest between sets, don't rush it.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.form_cue: Push hips back first, soft knee bend, dumbbells trace close down your legs. Stop the descent when your lower back wants to round.
exercises.why: The primary posterior chain lift in this session — hamstrings, glutes, and spinal control all get built here.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat (dumbbells)
exercises.form_cue: Back foot elevated on a bench, dumbbells at your sides. Drop straight down until the back knee nearly grazes the floor.
exercises.why: Single-leg strength closes the gap between your dominant and non-dominant side — a bilateral lift alone can't do that.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Step-Up
exercises.form_cue: Bench or box at about knee height. Drive through the planted heel to stand tall — don't push off the trailing foot.
exercises.why: Direct single-leg power that carries into running, jumping, and change-of-direction sports.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.form_cue: Elbows at roughly 45 degrees from your torso, not flared to 90. Press until your arms are straight but not locked hard.
exercises.why: Your primary horizontal press — chest, shoulders, and triceps under real load.

exercises.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.form_cue: Flat back braced on the bench, pull the dumbbell to your hip, elbow brushing your ribs.
exercises.why: Matches the pressing volume with pulling volume — keeps shoulders balanced and healthy under a real strength program.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Overhead Press
exercises.form_cue: Brace your core hard before you press — don't let your lower back arch to get the weight up.
exercises.why: Overhead strength and shoulder stability that most lower-body-focused programs neglect.

exercises.name: Weighted Dead Bug
exercises.form_cue: Hold a light dumbbell overhead with both hands. Lower back stays flat on the floor. Extend the opposite leg slow.
exercises.why: Anti-extension core control — protects your lower back on every heavy hinge and press in this program.

exercises.name: Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.form_cue: Back knee down, tuck your tailbone under, gently push the hips forward.
exercises.why: Split squats and step-ups tighten the hip flexors — undo that before you finish.

progression_notes: Add weight to the RDL first once 4x8 feels controlled — it's the anchor lift. Add a rep before adding weight on the split squat and step-up until both sides feel even.
